item.title: Contributed to the GLOHRA’s fact-finding mission to Brussels
item.description: I recently had the privilege of joining the Steering Committee of the German Alliance for Global Health Research (GLOHRA) in Brussels for a fact-finding mission from 17–20 November 2025. Alongside colleagues from diverse research disciplines, we engaged in constructive dialogue with key European institutions and partners to better understand the EU’s policy and funding landscape for global health research. Over three days of meetings, we gained valuable insights into emerging priorities for research funding and the upcoming EU Framework Programme (FP10), identifying new opportunities for collaboration and coordinated action from the research community. This visit not only strengthened our understanding of how global health research can be supported at the EU level but also reinforced our collective commitment to advancing impactful, interdisciplinary research that addresses global health challenges.

item.title: Contributed to the GLOHRA SC Meeting and GLOHRA Day in Berlin, Germany
item.description:
At this year’s GLOHRA Steering Committee Meeting and GLOHRA Day, I helped put AI’s real-world value for global health firmly on the agenda. Co-leading the SC round-table with Prof. Charlotte Koehler, I steered debate away from hype toward actionable next steps. Later, at the Bundestag Parliamentary Evening, we participated in an interesting veent on Global Health in LMICs.

The next day, Jana Fehr and I ran an “Ask the Community” session to crowd-source how we should measure impactful AI. Participants mapped indicators for health outcomes, equity, and system sustainability, then agreed to co-develop a mixed-methods framework all projects can plug into—so evidence accumulates across diseases and settings. The experience clarified my role as a bridge between data science, health systems, and policy.

item.title: Participated at the GLOHRA Training on Public Affairs in Berlin, Germany
item.description:
What an amazing two days in Berlin! 🇩🇪 I joined the GLOHRA Steering Committee’s public affairs training, sharpening skills in stakeholder mapping, policy briefs, and advocacy pitches.Great to see GlobalHealth in the Koalitionsvertrag—now let’s 1) cut bureaucracy in funding, 2) use development budgets for research, and 3) build sustainable international partnerships

Thanks to Boris Barth, German Alliance for Global Health Research (GLOHRA), and all participants for their insights and enthusiasm!

item.title: Invited Lecture for the GLOHRA Academy Series
item.description: Join us in our #GLOHRA session on Federated Learning with Medical Imaging! This is quite an important topic nowadays to tackle the data privacy issue while leveraging the collective intelligence we have in multi-national and diverse medical institutes around the globe! It is the way forward to bridge the gap between the global north and global south in medicine and healthcare! This aligns with our recent activities in organizing the 5th workshop on Collaborative and Federated Learning which will happen in Morocco in conjunction with MICCAI, and our recent IEEE-TMI Special Issue on Federated Learning. I am looking forward to meeting you on 1st October!
